chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Bird as a model; Collins on smoking pot
summary: Collins heard Parker play worse when high; for himself pot was an escape from being poor, until he stopped when it hindered his playing.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, sure they did. Sure, I've heard -- I've had -- like Stan Levy told me that Bird -- Bird was like Jezebel. He led everybody, you know. Because not that he consciously tried to do this, but they just were followers, you know. They would do anything he did. You know. So -- but I knew a lot of musicians who were great musicians, didn't touch it. But it's a funny thing, I can tell you -- I hear records that Bird made, and I knew that he was high. And I heard other records that he wasn't high and he played beautifully. But when he was really out of it you could tell it on his record. He wasn't playing as well.
How about smoking pot. Do you think that is a freeing influence in music?
I don't know. No, it didn't help me. For me it was an escape.

Being poor, you know, so I could laugh, you know, and it wouldn't bother me. That was really why I smoked pot. But it came -- once I got to a certain point I just stopped because I realized that it wasn't helping me, you know, it was more or less hindering me. I didn't play as well, you know. I enjoyed playing more but I wasn't playing as well. You know.
And then I think that some people are biologically or chemically stronger than others. I really believe this. Now, there are some guys who probably can handle it. They are --
